results.title: Healthcare Marketing Trends In 2025 – 2026: Strategies Shaping The Future
results.content: Healthcare marketing trends in 2025 are signaling a seismic shift in the industry. Patients are no longer passive consumers; they are active decision-makers who expect the same convenience, transparency, and personalization they get from top retail and tech brands. In 2025–2026, we predict this evolution accelerates. AI-powered personalization, privacy-first engagement, integrated patient journeys, and immersive experiences are redefining how healthcare providers attract and retain patients. Hospitals, clinics, and specialty practices that embrace these trends early will build stronger trust, improve patient outcomes, and dominate local and national markets. This report breaks down the top 2025–2026 healthcare marketing trends and provides real-world strategies and examples to help you:. * Build long-term trust through ethical, compliant marketing. * Integrate marketing with revenue and patient experience workflows. ## Top Healthcare Marketing Trends for 2025–2026. 1. AI-Powered Personalization and Predictive Marketing. 2. Privacy-First Healthcare Marketing Trends. By 2026, AI in healthcare marketing moves beyond personalization into predictive engagement, allowing providers to anticipate patient needs before they arise.

results.title: Journal of Medical Internet Research - Multidisciplinary Contributions and Research Trends in eHealth Scholarship (2000-2024): Bibliometric Analysis
results.content: Multidisciplinary Contributions and Research Trends in eHealth Scholarship (2000-2024): Bibliometric Analysis: Bibliometric Analysis"). To that end, we analyze evidence from 3 corpora: 10,022 OpenAlex documents with eHealth in the title, the 5000 most relevant eHealth articles according to the Web of Science (WoS) algorithm, and all available (n=1885) WoS eHealth reviews. Results: Several research directions emerged from bibliometric networks: eHealth studies on self-management and interventions, especially in mental health; telemedicine, telehealth, and technology acceptance; privacy, security, and design concerns; health information consumers’ literacy; health promotion and prevention; mHealth and digital health; and HIV prevention. Keywords such as *internet* (mean publication year 2017), *telemedicine* (2018), *telehealth* (2018), *mHealth* (2019), *mobile health* (2020), and *digital health* (2021) were strongly linked to literature indexed with *eHealth* (2019). Review authors cited a wide range of medical sources and journals specific to eHealth technologies, as well as journals in psychology, psychiatry, public health, policy, education, health communication, and other fields.
